exponential_background — VIDEOSTREAM recursive op

• Data kinds: video → video

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.exponential_background(video, alpha: 'float' = 0.05) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import videostream; videostream.exponential_background(video, alpha: 'float' = 0.05) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsvideostream.get("exponential_background"))

Usage

Recursive background bg ← (1−α)·bg + α·frame per frame → (T, H, W) (video).

An exponential moving average that initialises bg with the first frame and then repeats bg += α (frame - bg) per pixel. The state is just 1 background (no window). The output for frame t is a copy of bg at that moment, and t = 0 is the first input frame itself.

• video: a (T, H, W) array or a list of 2-D frames. Integer dtypes are normalised to [0, 1] by their maximum, float is clipped to [0, 1]. NaN/Inf gives ValueError.

• alpha: [0, 1]. The time constant is roughly 1/α frames (0.05 → about 20 frames). With 0 the background stays fixed at the first frame, with 1 it is always the current frame. When an object stops, it is absorbed into the background in about 1/α frames (there is no selective update).

• Returns: (T, H, W) float64, [0, 1].

• Failure: ValueError (shape, dtype, range of alpha).

If you also want the foreground mask, exponential_foreground uses the same model. To match the threshold to the per-pixel noise, running_gaussian_background.
